headline: Germany revises Q3 GDP growth downward to 0.1%
summary: The German Federal Statistical Office revised third-quarter GDP growth to 0.1% from the initial estimate of 0.2%. The adjustment reflects a slightly weaker economic performance than previously anticipated.
why: Germany is the largest economy in the Eurozone. Revisions to its growth data are closely watched by investors for signs of stagnation or recovery in the European industrial base.

impacts.name: DAX
impacts.why: Weaker-than-expected GDP growth data often weighs on domestic equity markets.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The downward revision signals that the German economy is growing more slowly than initially thought, dampening investor sentiment.
